rationale: The last two wins suggest the exact metric is now limited by late-step noise in tensors that survive the final artifact in float. This keeps the current best architecture and quant-aware endgame, but gives large 2D float-kept tensors such as the embedding table, bigram head, and rescued tail projections a slower EMA than small/control tensors. The hypothesis is that those matrices want a longer averaging window while q-gains, skip weights, and other control vectors should stay on the current faster decay. I also remove the redundant pre-save roundtrip when the EMA path is going to overwrite it anyway, keeping the script lean and slightly cheaper at the end.
title: Split-Rate EMA For Float-Kept Matrices
